suppress.notes:
False positive, not a real exposure here. CVE-2026-53914 ("Code execution was possible via unsafe deserialization in the build cache metadata") is a JetBrains Kotlin *compiler*/build-tool vulnerability (CWE-502, deserializing untrusted Gradle/Kotlin build-cache metadata) — confirmed against the CVE's own NVD description and JetBrains' own security bulletin (https://www.jetbrains.com/privacy-security/issues-fixed/) before suppressing, not assumed.
dependency-check's CPE analyzer matches the broad `cpe:2.3:a:jetbrains:kotlin:*` product identifier against `kotlin-stdlib`, but this project never compiles Kotlin code and never invokes a Kotlin/Gradle build cache — kotlin-stdlib.jar ships none of the vulnerable compiler code, only runtime helper classes. The actual dependency path is transitive and purely runtime: resilience4j-circuitbreaker (added for P2.4's external-HTTP-dependency circuit breakers) -> resilience4j-core -> kotlin-stdlib-jdk8 -> kotlin-stdlib, consumed only as an already-compiled runtime jar.
Not fixed by excluding kotlin-stdlib outright: resilience4j-core 2.3.0's own implementation is partially written in Kotlin and genuinely calls into kotlin-stdlib at runtime — removing it risks a real NoClassDefFoundError on that code path, trading a false-positive CVE for an actual production defect. Not fixed by a version bump either: the vulnerability lives in the Kotlin compiler tooling, not in any kotlin-stdlib runtime API surface, so no kotlin-stdlib version pin changes the real exposure here.
